minutes.headline: Capital committee voted Marshall Park next in line for any extra FY22 capital money; threshold change left for March 2
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed the FY22 capital plan, including revised Town Hall and Ritter building estimates, and agreed by voice vote that Marshall Park is next on the list if more capital money becomes available. It then discussed the Finance Committee's request to review capital-related fiscal policy, chiefly raising the dollar threshold for capital projects, without settling on a number. A follow-up meeting was set for March 2nd.

votes.motion: If more money becomes available, Marshall Park would be next on the list

budget_items.topic: Town Hall and Ritter building project estimates
budget_items.what_was_said: Revised estimates came in; Town Hall slightly higher, covered partly by a chimney work item, while Ritter came in significantly higher. Ritter could be bid with alternates.
Members checked the base bid sum against the spreadsheet and the earlier estimate and agreed the base bid is below the recommended project cost.
Leftover funds would return to the capital plan only after full project closure, since paving remains.
The committee discussed raising the threshold from the current level, with 30,000 proposed, and a staged increase was floated.
The vests are the number two priority and the department could not absorb them in its budget, raising the concern of where money comes from if the threshold rises.
Capital draws on free cash, raise and appropriate, stabilization and borrowing; operating budget does not use free cash.

decisions.decision: Next meeting set for March 2nd to continue the fiscal policy review.
Committee will review the selectmen's fiscal policy capital section and send a recommendation to the Finance Committee.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee agreed by voice vote that Marshall Park is next on the list if more FY22 capital money becomes available.
Members reviewed revised Town Hall and Ritter building estimates; Ritter came in significantly higher and could be bid with alternates.
Members checked the Ritter base bid against the spreadsheet and agreed it is below the recommended project cost.
The committee will review the selectmen's capital fiscal policy and send a recommendation to the Finance Committee; a higher project dollar threshold was discussed without a settled figure.
Leftover underground storage tank funds return to the capital plan only after full project closure, since paving remains.

why_it_matters: Raising the dollar threshold for what counts as a capital project could shift items such as police vests from the capital plan into department operating budgets, which are paid mostly from taxes.
The Ritter estimate and the Marshall Park ranking show which building and park work could be funded first from free cash, borrowing or other capital sources.
